What TypeScript static analysis, type-level safety, and compile-time protection mechanisms should an OpenAPI SDK wrapper use? Research the state of the art in 2025-2026 for: (1) Type-safe API client patterns - branded types, phantom types, tagged unions for API responses, template literal types for URL path construction, conditional types for auth-gated endpoints; (2) OpenAPI-to-TypeScript code generation best practices - openapi-typescript, openapi-fetch, zodios, fets, feTS, ts-rest, orval, hey-api; (3) Static analysis beyond ESLint - TypeScript compiler plugins, ts-morph for custom checks, API surface linting with api-extractor, knip for dead exports; (4) Zod and runtime validation integration with static types - zod inference, ensuring schema-type alignment at compile time; (5) Type-level testing approaches - tsd, expect-type, @type-challenges patterns; (6) Contract testing at the type level - ensuring SDK types match OpenAPI spec at build time; (7) Dependency injection and configuration type safety patterns; (8) Error handling type safety - discriminated unions, Result/Either patterns, typed error codes. "Hey API's Zod v4 plugin generates three categories of Zod schemas from OpenAPI specs: request schemas (headers, path params, query params as separate objects), response schemas (single schema per endpoint, using z.union for multiple responses), and definition schemas (one per reusable OpenAPI component schema)."

1. Is the claim actually supported by the quote, or is it an overreach/misread?

5. Is this a marketing claim / press release / cherry-picked benchmark / forum speculation?

**refuted=false** ONLY if: claim is well-supported, current, and source quality matches claim strength.
